title: Sudanese Anti-War Forces Reject Burhan's Dialogue Call, Adopt Alternative Peace Roadmap in Addis Ababa
detail: August 22-23, 2026 — A broad coalition of Sudanese anti-war political parties, civil society organizations and public figures — including forces behind the Sudanese Declaration of Principles, the Popular Congress Party, and a faction of the Umma Party led by Mubarak al-Fadil, alongside women's and youth networks — met for two days in Addis Ababa and rejected army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan's Aug 14 offer to convene an in-country national dialogue, dismissing it as a manoeuvre to entrench military rule and pave the way for elements of the former regime and Islamist movement to return to power. Sumoud Coalition head and former PM Abdalla Hamdok, Sudan Liberation Movement leader Abdel Wahid al-Nur, and Baath Party figure Wajdi Saleh attended. Participants adopted a joint position paper, "The Peace Process We Want," reaffirming support for the September 2025 Quadrilateral Roadmap and calling for a fully civilian-led political process built around three parallel tracks — humanitarian access, a permanent ceasefire, and an exclusively civilian transition — alongside unified international mediation.
